{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfy2hhpj1nrx8xqqi5YNc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The matmul benchmark now runs its initialization and multiply in parallel with OpenMP, and the result is bit-identical to a strict-IEEE run of the original code. At N=2048 it went from 0.17 GFLOPS to 337 GFLOPS on this 256-core machine.\n\n**What changed** (only `matmul/matmul.cpp` and `matmul/CMakeLists.txt`; no new files, executable name unchanged):\n\n- **`initMatrix`**: `#pragma omp parallel for` over rows.\n- **`matrixMultiply`**: parallel over blocks of 4 rows of C, with 64×64 k/j tiles for cache reuse. Each `C[i][j]` still sums over `k` in ascending order, so the summation order is the same as the original.\n- **`CMakeLists.txt`**: `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and link `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`, so OpenMP is always used and configure fails if it is missing. I also added `-ffp-contract=off` (explained below).\n- `validateResult` and the output code are unchanged and remain serial. The check is 25 dot products, so there is nothing to gain.\n\n**Correctness:**\n- With the original compiled under `-ffp-contract=off`, the new binary's `-r` output (Sum, Min, Max, samples, Hash) matches exactly for N = 1, 2, 3, 7, 63, 64, 65, 129, 333, 512, 1000, at 1, 4 and 256 threads.\n- `-v` validation passes.\n\n**Decision for you: `-ffp-contract=off`.** Without it, the original's default build was not reproducible in a way I could match. GCC vectorized its `k` reduction with unfused multiply+add in one part and used FMA in the scalar tail. The new loop's fusing differed, so the hashes differed in the last bits at some sizes (e.g. N=7, 333). Turning contraction off makes the output deterministic and equal to the strict reference. The cost is that outputs will differ in the last bits from a binary built without that flag. If you would rather keep FMA throughput and accept the last-bit differences, remove that flag.\n\n**Other notes:**\n- `N=0 -v` crashes with a floating-point exception in both the original and the new binary, because `validateResult` takes `% N`. I left it alone since it's outside the parallelization scope.\n- Build and measurement were done in /tmp so no build artifacts landed in the project."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":382,"cache_read_input_tokens":33945,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":382},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"efb55340-106b-4296-9de8-fbf65b25163a","uuid":"72836595-8a4f-4ee8-b505-a766dd92f052","timestamp":"2026-10-12T21:11:05.101Z","request_id":"req_011Cfy2hhVdefeX7TDRU7SzA"}
